title: Get Beyond Learning Styles
heading: Get Beyond Learning Styles
coreClaim: The chapter argues that style matching is not the main route to stronger learning and that better design fits the material, checks prior knowledge, and uses active retrieval or explanation.
distinctMechanism: The mechanism is evidence-backed fit: choosing representations because they serve the content and building active processing into the lesson rather than chasing style labels.
requiredAnchors: Preference is not proof of stronger learning.
Prior knowledge and active processing matter more than style labels.
commonMisreadings: Learner differences do not matter at all.
The chapter rejects visual, verbal, or hands-on tools entirely.
specificApplications: Choose diagrams, words, or demonstrations because the content calls for them.
Check background knowledge before blaming a style mismatch.
Build retrieval and explanation into lessons.
hardEdgeRequirement: Reject the myth without collapsing into one-size-fits-all teaching.
thresholdQuestion: What should guide instruction if not a simple style label?
